transfer_rates.weights: PyCHAM class-centre run, particle-phase mass at 6 h

mismatches.what: Operator split. TOMAS-JAX integrates chemistry for one coupling interval, then partitions the vapour formed over the same interval (A12). PyCHAM solves chemistry and partitioning in one ODE, rates refreshed every 60 s.
mismatches.why: Driver design; the interval is a model setting.
mismatches.effect: Vapour formed during an interval gets the whole interval to condense, so SOA runs ahead early: +13.3 % at 30 min, +4.2 % at 1 h with 300 s coupling; +8.6 % and +3.9 % at 60 s. 60 s vs 300 s coupling differ by +0.25 % at 6 h.

mismatches.what: Gas-to-particle transfer rate. vbs-jax: Fuller D with one diffusion volume (120) and the class-mean MW, mfp = 2D/c, Zaveri et al. (2014) Fuchs-Sutugin. PyCHAM: each species' own diffusion volume from SMILES (~200-235), mfp = 3D/c, Jacobson (2005) form.
mismatches.effect: On the same size distribution PyCHAM's organic condensation sink is 0.69x ours at t = 0 (0.71x at 6 h sizes; diffusivity alone 0.79x). With our sink scaled by 0.69 (and 60 s coupling) the SOA difference is +3.1 % at 30 min and +2.4 % at 1 h.

mismatches.what: Raoult convention: organic-phase mass fraction (TOMAS-JAX, soacond) vs mole fraction (PyCHAM). The seed-OA MW (232.3 g/mol) is close to the number-mean SOA MW to keep them close.
mismatches.effect: PyCHAM with mass-fraction Raoult ('massfrac': one MW in the c* -> Pa conversion) has +1.2 % to +1.6 % more SOA than with mole fraction.

mismatches.what: Kelvin term. vbs-jax: sigma 0.025 N/m, rho_org 1200 kg/m3, class MW, wet Dp. PyCHAM: sigma 0.072 N/m, mass-weighted mean particle MW (incl. water and sulfate), particle density; it also applies Kelvin to water.
mismatches.effect: Kelvin lowers SOA by 0.83 % in TOMAS-JAX and 1.3 % in PyCHAM at 6 h (2.4 % / 3.8 % at 30 min). With transfer and Raoult matched the SOA difference is -0.07 % to +1.5 % with Kelvin on and -0.54 % to -0.01 % with Kelvin off in both (patched PyCHAM copy, vbs-jax sigma = 0).

mismatches.what: Within-class species identity. TOMAS-JAX partitions c* classes and hands the class change to species with a tracker (ClassBridge.scatter); PyCHAM is explicit per species.
mismatches.effect: Members of one class should have one particle fraction; class log c* = 0.5 at 6 h: PyCHAM 0.81-0.83, TOMAS-JAX 0.29-0.94. Per-species particle and gas masses of condensables differ accordingly; class totals are robust.

mismatches.what: Sectional numerics: TOMAS two-moment fixed bins (SOA growth and evaporation move particles with the PPM log-mass remap, AerosolStepConfig.growth_bin_transfer = 'ppm') vs PyCHAM moving centre on the same 40-bin grid.
mismatches.effect: At 6 h, from each bin's mean dry size: number-mean dry diameter 213.8 (TOMAS-JAX) vs 210.1 nm (PyCHAM, +1.8 %), GSD 1.362 vs 1.411 (-3.5 %), dry-mass-weighted mean 276.5 vs 281.7 nm; particles below the seed's 1st-percentile diameter 0.16 % vs 0.05 %. PyCHAM bins merge, so its curve is spiky. Number and mass are conserved in both.

mismatches.what: Particle water. TOMAS-JAX: ezwatereqm, 0.3470 kg water per kg SO4 (NH4HSO4 ratio x 1.2) and 0.2891 per kg of any organic (A9); no Kelvin term. PyCHAM: ideal solution with per-component dissociation constants (SA 1.8905, SEEDOA 3.7310, condensables 1.703-4.837) that give TOMAS-JAX's water per unit mass of each component when Kelvin = 1, plus its Kelvin term on water.
mismatches.why: PyCHAM has no fixed hygroscopic-growth input; its water always feels Kelvin.
mismatches.effect: PyCHAM water relative to TOMAS-JAX: -9.0 % at 0h, -12.2 % at 1h, -9.7 % at 3h, -8.7 % at 6h (Kelvin on water). With Kelvin off in both (attribution pair): -0.00 % at 0h, -0.56 % at 1h, +0.41 % at 6h.

mismatches.what: Densities. TOMAS-JAX: Tang (1997) H2SO4-solution density, organics counted as sulfate (wet seed 1682 kg/m3). PyCHAM: additive volumes, 2170 kg/m3 for every non-water component (chosen so the wet seed volume matches at t = 0) and 1000 for water.
mismatches.effect: Same wet volume at t = 0. On TOMAS-JAX's bulk composition at 6 h the two rules give 1704 vs 1713 kg/m3 (+0.54 %, about +0.18 % in diameter for the same mass).

mismatches.what: Seed sulfate identity. PyCHAM's seed component SA is H2SO4 (SMILES MW 98.08) and receives TOMAS-JAX's SO4-slot mass; TOMAS-JAX treats that mass as SO4 (MW 96) and as NH4HSO4 (x 1.2) for water.
mismatches.why: PyCHAM needs a SMILES; there is no bisulfate component.
mismatches.effect: Mass identical; moles differ by 2 %. Enters PyCHAM's mass-mean MW in its Kelvin term (sulfate is not in the absorbing phase in either model). Water is matched per unit mass. Expected effect on SOA: negligible.

mismatches.what: Volatility input. PyCHAM gets volP = the TOMAS-JAX class-centre c*(298.15 K) of every condensable species, converted with PyCHAM's own MW, constant in T. Non-condensables get 1e5 Pa (ppartit_cutoff 100 Pa); SA and the seed OA 1e-20 Pa.
mismatches.why: Like-for-like test of the partitioning numerics.
mismatches.effect: Exact by construction (checked to 4e-11). S2 therefore tests partitioning and transport for identical volatility; it does not test the Li et al. (2016) c* (A8). With PyCHAM's own vapour pressures the SOA is 0.51x the class-centre run at 6 h and its N-containing share 5 % (class-centre 98 %), so the NOx-sink feedback is an A8 consequence.

mismatches.what: c* lumping: TOMAS-JAX half-decade classes vs PyCHAM explicit species at the class-centre c* (main run) or at each species' own Li c* ('exact').
mismatches.effect: PyCHAM own c* vs class centre: +10.7 % at 30 min, +7.0 % at 1 h, +1.2 % at 6 h.

mismatches.what: Seed and bins. TOMAS-JAX bins 4-32 go to PyCHAM (every bin with N0 >= 1e-6 cm-3 plus 4 empty bins on top), bounds at the wet-volume radii of the dry-mass edges; SEEDOA (6-hydroxyundecanedioic acid) is a stand-in molecule added through a dead reaction.
mismatches.why: PyCHAM needs a component with a SMILES; tiny bins only add stiffness.
mismatches.effect: 1.3e-06 cm-3 of seed left out; t = 0 number and dry mass identical to 1e-6.

mismatches.what: H2SO4: TOMAS-JAX turns the SA counter into an H2SO4 source for TOMAS condensation; PyCHAM SA gas condenses in its ODE with vp 1e-20 Pa.
mismatches.effect: Sulfate added by 6 h: 0.0523 vs 0.0522 ug/m3.

mismatches.what: Particle-phase diffusion: two-film with D_b = 1e-10 m2/s (vbs-jax) vs well mixed (PyCHAM).
mismatches.effect: Negligible (< 4e-5 of the gas-side resistance at c* = 1e4 and 100 nm).

mismatches.what: Gas phase as in G2: rates/J/RO2 frozen per interval, solver tolerances, Buck vs Hyland-Wexler water vapour, SA/PROD/NA bookkeeping, <34> rate 0.
mismatches.effect: Without particles the S2 set-ups agree like G2.

mismatches.what: Processes off in both: coagulation, nucleation, N2O5 uptake (gamma = 0).
mismatches.effect: The preset has coagulation on; S2 does not test it.
